meta.description: Combat Talents (Kampftechnik-Talente) from TDE 4.1. These talents govern attack and parry values rather than standard talent tests. TP is split between AT and PA (except jousting/ranged which use AT only). Fallback penalty: -5 total (AT-2, PA-3).

talents.name: Axes and Maces
talents.description: Covers all one-handed blunt weapons — axes (with broad blade on a haft), maces, clubs, war hammers, and similar weapons whose damage comes primarily from blunt force, concentrating force on a point to dent armor or break bones. Maximum length approximately one pace, maximum weight approximately three stone.

talents.name: Bastard Sword
talents.description: Covers bastard swords (anderthalbhänder) and Tuzak knives. The defining feature is the quick switch between one-handed and two-handed grip and back — hence the name 'one-and-a-half-handed'. Despite considerable weight, a well-handled bastard sword allows nearly as varied a blade style as fencing weapons, which is why this talent is regarded as the 'royal discipline' of blade weapons. A shield or parrying weapon cannot be carried simultaneously.

talents.name: Bow
talents.description: Covers all bow types: short bow, composite bow, war bow, long bow, elf bow. Bows are the weapon of choice for steppe, desert, and meadow dwellers. Both elves and orks, Weideners and Novadis are known for their bow skills. Whenever a hit with an arrow deals more than CN/2-2 damage points, it inflicts a wound.

talents.name: Brawling
talents.description: The skill of causing damage through use of hands, feet, and teeth — punches, straights, claw blows, head butts, bites, knee strikes, and spinning jump kicks all fall under this talent — or avoiding such attacks by blocking, dodging, sidestepping, and similar techniques. Attacks with bare hands or feet normally deal 1d6 HP (ED): these points are deducted from Endurance, with half also deducted from VP.

talents.name: Chain Weapons
talents.description: Weapons where a ball or other heavy weight, usually spiked, is attached to the end of a chain whose length is just under that of the handle. These weapons are difficult to parry but also difficult to block — they can strike around shields and are generally hard to deflect. Chain weapons ignore the PA bonus provided by shields. Blocking a chain weapon attack is more difficult (+2) for all weapons capable of parrying one.

talents.name: Crossbow
talents.description: All crossbow-type weapons have a stock, trigger, and cocking mechanism and are fired by aiming and pulling the trigger. Whenever a crossbow bolt deals more than CN/2-2 damage points, it inflicts a wound (except for ball-firing ballistae, which use the normal CN/2 threshold).

talents.name: Daggers
talents.description: Covers all stabbing (and rarely parrying) blade weapons with a maximum total length of half a pace — from the eating knife used as a weapon to the long dagger whose largest examples could almost be called a short sword. Nearly all daggers have a straight, double-edged blade. Attacks from chain weapons, two-handed blunt weapons, and two-handed swords cannot be parried with a dagger.

talents.name: Fencing Weapons
talents.description: Narrow, nearly exclusively thrusting blade weapons with a blade length of just under a pace, usually with richly decorated basket hilts, parrying bars, or intricately twisted parrying rods. They are elegant, fast, and considered 'modern' by some and 'ridiculous coxcomb weapons' by others. With a rapier, blows from chain weapons and two-handed blunt weapons cannot be parried; with a foil, also not attacks from two-handed swords.

talents.name: Infantry Weapons
talents.description: Weapons with a short blade mounted on a long haft, suitable for both hewing and thrusting; sometimes with hooks to knock opponents down or pull them off horses. These are two-handed weapons approximately two and a half paces long; simultaneous use of a shield is not possible. In ranged-distance combat rules, infantry weapons are usually in the pole-weapon range.

talents.name: Jousting
talents.description: Represents the cavalry charge with a couched lance. This is a pure attack talent, handled similarly to ranged combat — all TP go to the AT value. It is impossible to parry with a couched lance. Used for tournament lances as well as war lances.

talents.name: Sabers
talents.description: In contrast to swords, these weapons are primarily used for slashing and rarely for thrusting, and they usually have only one cutting edge (and possibly a worked tip). This category ranges from short cutlasses to elegant cavalry sabers to heavy, almost axe-like weapons.

talents.name: Spears
talents.description: Spears are weapons of maximum 2 paces length used exclusively for thrusting; the parry is typically done with the blunt end (if one even parries with a spear). One-handed spears can be thrown (two-handed ones as well, but usually with unimpressive results). One-handed and two-handed variants exist.

talents.name: Staves
talents.description: A simple wooden staff approximately eight spans long can be an effective weapon in the hands of a master — and combat staves are usually not 'simple wooden weapons' but specially hardened, wound with metal bands, or even with blades at both ends. Staves are two-handed weapons; simultaneous use of a shield is not possible.

talents.name: Swords
talents.description: Blade weapons with a total length of half to one-and-a-quarter paces, of which the double-edged blade makes up at least three-quarters. Swords are intended for both cutting and thrusting; their crossguard allows more demanding defensive maneuvers.

talents.name: Throwing Axes
talents.description: This ranged weapon, especially common among pirates like the Thorwalians, is difficult to handle because it rotates around its transverse axis during flight. Most throwing axes are 'sharp on all edges' and made entirely of metal. Also used for all tumbling throwing clubs and throwing sticks.

talents.name: Throwing Knives
talents.description: Knives and daggers are the most widespread throwing weapons, but not every knife or dagger is suitable for throwing. Only specially balanced weapons — usually with a particularly light grip — are throwable. Throwing discs and rings also fall into this category, as do throwing darts and spines.

talents.name: Javelins
talents.description: The throwing spear/javelin is a hunting weapon used by all peoples and was once also used extensively in Aventurian armies. There are throwing spears in various sizes, and some are accelerated with short throwing sticks.

talents.name: Two-Handed Blunt Weapons
talents.description: These weapons require landing the heavy (and sometimes sharp) striking surface with great force precisely on target, since the haft does little damage; stabs and thrusts are not suitable with these weapons, and their parrying ability is also severely limited. These are two-handed weapons; simultaneous use of a shield is not possible.

talents.name: Two-Handed Swords
talents.description: These particularly long blade weapons are primarily intended for hewing, though they can also thrust at shorter range and still allow reasonable parries (although all actions are somewhat slower than with the universally usable bastard swords, which also fall into this category since they are used similarly). These are two-handed weapons; a shield cannot be used simultaneously.

talents.name: Wrestling
talents.description: Covers all techniques for grabbing an opponent, holding, gripping, throwing to the ground, or pinning, as well as defensive options against such attacks — from simply evading to actively freeing oneself (which can even be used to escape from the coils of a kraken or a snake). Wrestling attacks as a throw deal 1d6 HP (ED) or bring the opponent into an unfavorable position, facilitating subsequent attacks.

talents.name: Chain Staves
talents.description: Two round hardwood staves (approximately two spans each) connected by a chain of equal length. Requires minimum AG 15 to wield effectively. Ignores the PA bonus provided by shields. Disarming from the attack is 4 points easier. Converting attack actions into defense actions (from TP 10) is possible without penalty. The three-section staff (Dreigliederstab) is a variant with three shorter sections.

talents.name: Whip
talents.description: Pure attack talent — all talent points go to AT, no PA is derived from this talent (like jousting). The whip can disarm an opponent or knock them off their feet; it ignores the PA bonus of shields. Suffers an AT penalty of 8 points in close-quarters (Nahkampf) distance and cannot be used at all in grapple range (Handgemenge). The nine-tails (Neunschwänzige) is especially effective against swarms.

talents.name: Two-Handed Flails
talents.description: Two-handed weapons where a heavy striking piece is attached to a long haft by a chain or cord. These weapons are difficult to control but devastating — they ignore the PA bonus provided by shields. Two-handed weapons; a shield cannot be carried simultaneously.

talents.name: Sling
talents.description: Covers all sling-type ranged weapons including the standard sling, bola, lasso, fledermaus (weighted cord), and throwing nets. Several weapons in this category deal no direct damage but instead impose difficulty penalties on the target's escape check. Staff slings (Stabschleuder) cannot be used from horseback.

talents.name: Discus
talents.description: Flat disc-shaped throwing weapons of Maraskan origin, usually made of hardwood and often brightly decorated. The combat discus (Kampfdiskus) has a razor-sharp steel edge and requires a special throwing glove (15 S) and minimum ST 14. Some examples produce howling sounds in flight. Optional HP/ST damage scaling is available.

talents.name: Blowpipe
talents.description: Typical hunting weapon from southern Aventuria in which small darts are propelled by breath pressure. Darts are usually coated with poison (see poisons section). Blowpipes can only be used from horseback on a stationary mount.
